passages.text: This is what happened in the days of Xerxes, who reigned over 127 provinces from India to Cush.
passages.sermon:
Xerxes was king.
Xerxes ruled in ancient times.
He ruled over 127 provinces.
His kingdom stretched from India to Cush.
These events happened during his reign.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֖י בִּימֵ֣י אֲחַשְׁוֵר֑וֹשׁ ה֣וּא אֲחַשְׁוֵר֗וֹשׁ הַמֹּלֵךְ֙ מֵהֹ֣דּוּ וְעַד־ כּ֔וּשׁ שֶׁ֛בַע וְעֶשְׂרִ֥ים וּמֵאָ֖ה מְדִינָֽה׃

passages.text: In those days King Xerxes sat on his royal throne in the citadel of Susa.
passages.sermon: King Xerxes was the ruler at that time.\r\nHe sat on his royal throne.\r\nHis throne was in the citadel of Susa.
passages.original: בַּיָּמִ֖ים הָהֵ֑ם כְּשֶׁ֣בֶת׀ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵר֗וֹשׁ עַ֚ל כִּסֵּ֣א מַלְכוּת֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּשׁוּשַׁ֥ן הַבִּירָֽה׃

passages.text: In the third year of his reign, Xerxes held a feast for all his officials and servants. The military leaders of Persia and Media were there, along with the nobles and princes of the provinces.
passages.sermon:
King Xerxes ruled a vast empire.
He reigned over 127 provinces from India to Cush.
In the third year of his reign, King Xerxes gave a feast.
He invited all his officials and servants.
The military leaders of Persia and Media attended.
The nobles and princes of the provinces also came.
They all gathered before King Xerxes.
passages.original: בִּשְׁנַ֤ת שָׁלוֹשׁ֙ לְמָלְכ֔וֹ עָשָׂ֣ה מִשְׁתֶּ֔ה לְכָל־ שָׂרָ֖יו וַעֲבָדָ֑יו חֵ֣יל׀ פָּרַ֣ס וּמָדַ֗י הַֽפַּרְתְּמִ֛ים וְשָׂרֵ֥י הַמְּדִינ֖וֹת לְפָנָֽיו׃

passages.text: And for a full 180 days he displayed the glorious riches of his kingdom and the magnificent splendor of his greatness.
passages.sermon:
King Xerxes ruled in Susa.
He was a powerful king.
He had a great kingdom.
He was very rich.
He wanted to show his wealth.
He wanted to show his royal glory.
He wanted everyone to see his greatness.
He displayed his riches for many days.
He showed his splendor for 180 days.
He let people see the full beauty of his kingdom.
He let people see the greatness of his power.
passages.original: בְּהַרְאֹת֗וֹ אֶת־ עֹ֙שֶׁר֙ כְּב֣וֹד מַלְכוּת֔וֹ וְאֶ֨ת־ יְקָ֔ר תִּפְאֶ֖רֶת גְּדוּלָּת֑וֹ יָמִ֣ים רַבִּ֔ים שְׁמוֹנִ֥ים וּמְאַ֖ת יֽוֹם׃

passages.text: At the end of this time, in the garden court of the royal palace, the king held a seven-day feast for all the people in the citadel of Susa, from the least to the greatest.
passages.sermon:
King Xerxes ruled over Persia.
He lived in the citadel of Susa.
He finished a long celebration for his officials and nobles.
After this, he gave another feast.
He invited all the people in Susa.
He included everyone, from the least to the greatest.
He held the feast for seven days.
He hosted it in the garden court of his royal palace.
passages.original: וּבִמְל֣וֹאת׀ הַיָּמִ֣ים הָאֵ֗לֶּה עָשָׂ֣ה הַמֶּ֡לֶךְ לְכָל־ הָעָ֣ם הַנִּמְצְאִים֩ בְּשׁוּשַׁ֨ן הַבִּירָ֜ה לְמִגָּ֧דוֹל וְעַד־ קָטָ֛ן מִשְׁתֶּ֖ה שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֑ים בַּחֲצַ֕ר גִּנַּ֥ת בִּיתַ֖ן הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: Hangings of white and blue linen were fastened with cords of fine white and purple material to silver rings on the marble pillars. Gold and silver couches were arranged on a mosaic pavement of porphyry, marble, mother-of-pearl, and other costly stones.
passages.sermon:
King Xerxes ruled in the citadel of Susa.
He held a great feast in his royal palace.
White linen hangings decorated the area.
Blue linen hangings also decorated the area.
People fastened these hangings with cords of fine white material.
They also used cords of purple material.
Silver rings held the cords in place.
The rings were attached to marble pillars.
Gold couches stood in the court.
Silver couches also stood in the court.
The couches rested on a mosaic pavement.
The pavement was made of porphyry.
It was also made of marble.
It included mother-of-pearl.
It included other costly stones.
passages.original: ח֣וּר׀ כַּרְפַּ֣ס וּתְכֵ֗לֶת אָחוּז֙ בְּחַבְלֵי־ ב֣וּץ וְאַרְגָּמָ֔ן עַל־ גְּלִ֥ילֵי כֶ֖סֶף וְעַמּ֣וּדֵי שֵׁ֑שׁ מִטּ֣וֹת׀ זָהָ֣ב וָכֶ֗סֶף עַ֛ל רִֽצְפַ֥ת בַּהַט־ וָשֵׁ֖שׁ וְדַ֥ר וְסֹחָֽרֶת׃

passages.text: Beverages were served in an array of goblets of gold, each with a different design, and the royal wine flowed freely, according to the king’s bounty.
passages.sermon:
The king of Persia was very wealthy and generous.
He held a great feast in his royal palace.
Servants brought drinks to the guests.
They used many gold goblets.
Each goblet had a different design.
The king provided much royal wine.
The wine flowed freely for everyone.
The king gave as much as anyone wanted.
passages.original: וְהַשְׁקוֹת֙ בִּכְלֵ֣י זָהָ֔ב וְכֵלִ֖ים מִכֵּלִ֣ים שׁוֹנִ֑ים וְיֵ֥ין מַלְכ֛וּת רָ֖ב כְּיַ֥ד הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: By order of the king, no limit was placed on the drinking, and every official of his household was to serve each man whatever he desired.
passages.sermon:
King Xerxes gave an order about the drinking at the banquet.
He set no limit on how much anyone could drink.
He told every official in his household to serve each man as much as he wanted.
Each person could choose for himself how much to drink.
No one forced anyone to drink more or less than he wished.
passages.original: וְהַשְּׁתִיָּ֥ה כַדָּ֖ת אֵ֣ין אֹנֵ֑ס כִּי־ כֵ֣ן׀ יִסַּ֣ד הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ עַ֚ל כָּל־ רַ֣ב בֵּית֔וֹ לַעֲשׂ֖וֹת כִּרְצ֥וֹן אִישׁ־ וָאִֽישׁ׃

passages.text: Queen Vashti also gave a banquet for the women in the royal palace of King Xerxes.
passages.sermon:
Queen Vashti was the queen.
She gave a banquet.
She invited the women.
She held the banquet in the royal palace.
King Xerxes owned the palace.
passages.original: גַּ֚ם וַשְׁתִּ֣י הַמַּלְכָּ֔ה עָשְׂתָ֖ה מִשְׁתֵּ֣ה נָשִׁ֑ים בֵּ֚ית הַמַּלְכ֔וּת אֲשֶׁ֖ר לַמֶּ֥לֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרֽוֹשׁ׃ס

passages.text: On the seventh day, when the king’s heart was merry with wine, he ordered the seven eunuchs who served him—Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, Abagtha, Zethar, and Carkas— to bring Queen Vashti before him, wearing her royal crown, to display her beauty to the people and officials. For she was beautiful to behold.
passages.sermon:
King Xerxes ruled over Persia and Media.
He held a great banquet in his royal palace.
On the seventh day of the feast, the king felt happy because of the wine.
King Xerxes gave an order.
He spoke to seven eunuchs who served him.
Their names were Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, Abagtha, Zethar, and Carkas.
The king told them to bring Queen Vashti to him.
He wanted her to come wearing her royal crown.
He wanted to show her beauty to all the people and the officials.
Queen Vashti was very beautiful.
passages.original: בַּיּוֹם֙ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י כְּט֥וֹב לֵב־ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ בַּיָּ֑יִן אָמַ֡ר לִ֠מְהוּמָן בִּזְּתָ֨א חַרְבוֹנָ֜א בִּגְתָ֤א וַאֲבַגְתָא֙ זֵתַ֣ר וְכַרְכַּ֔ס שִׁבְעַת֙ הַסָּ֣רִיסִ֔ים הַמְשָׁ֣רְתִ֔ים אֶת־ פְּנֵ֖י הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרֽוֹשׁ׃ לְ֠הָבִיא אֶת־ וַשְׁתִּ֧י הַמַּלְכָּ֛ה לִפְנֵ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ בְּכֶ֣תֶר מַלְכ֑וּת לְהַרְא֨וֹת הָֽעַמִּ֤ים וְהַשָּׂרִים֙ אֶת־ יָפְיָ֔הּ כִּֽי־ טוֹבַ֥ת מַרְאֶ֖ה הִֽיא׃

passages.text: Queen Vashti, however, refused to come at the king’s command brought by his eunuchs. And the king became furious, and his anger burned within him.
passages.sermon:
Queen Vashti was the wife of King Xerxes.
The king sent his eunuchs to bring Queen Vashti to him.
Queen Vashti refused to come when the king commanded her.
The king became very angry.
His anger burned inside him.
passages.original: וַתְּמָאֵ֞ן הַמַּלְכָּ֣ה וַשְׁתִּ֗י לָבוֹא֙ בִּדְבַ֣ר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּיַ֣ד הַסָּרִיסִ֑ים וַיִּקְצֹ֤ף הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ מְאֹ֔ד וַחֲמָת֖וֹ בָּעֲרָ֥ה בֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Then the king consulted the wise men who knew the times, for it was customary for him to confer with the experts in law and justice.
passages.sermon:
King Xerxes ruled a vast kingdom.
He faced a difficult situation with Queen Vashti.
King Xerxes needed advice.
He spoke to his wise men.
These wise men understood the times.
They were experts in law and justice.
King Xerxes always consulted these experts.
He brought his question before all who knew the law and judgment.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לַחֲכָמִ֖ים יֹדְעֵ֣י הָֽעִתִּ֑ים כִּי־ כֵן֙ דְּבַ֣ר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לִפְנֵ֕י כָּל־ יֹדְעֵ֖י דָּ֥ת וָדִֽין׃

passages.text: His closest advisors were Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan, the seven princes of Persia and Media who had personal access to the king and ranked highest in the kingdom.
passages.sermon:
King Xerxes had seven closest advisors.
Their names were Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan.
These men were princes of Persia and Media.
They had personal access to the king.
They ranked highest in the kingdom.
passages.original: וְהַקָּרֹ֣ב אֵלָ֗יו כַּרְשְׁנָ֤א שֵׁתָר֙ אַדְמָ֣תָא תַרְשִׁ֔ישׁ מֶ֥רֶס מַרְסְנָ֖א מְמוּכָ֑ן שִׁבְעַ֞ת שָׂרֵ֣י׀ פָּרַ֣ס וּמָדַ֗י רֹאֵי֙ פְּנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ הַיֹּשְׁבִ֥ים רִאשֹׁנָ֖ה בַּמַּלְכֽוּת׃

passages.text: “According to law,” he asked, “what should be done with Queen Vashti, since she refused to obey the command of King Xerxes delivered by the eunuchs?”
passages.sermon:
King Xerxes was the ruler of Persia and Media.
He had a queen named Vashti.
King Xerxes gave a command to Queen Vashti.
The king sent this command through his eunuchs.
Queen Vashti refused to obey the king’s command.
King Xerxes asked his wise men a question.
He said, “According to the law, what should be done with Queen Vashti?”
He asked this because Queen Vashti did not do what King Xerxes commanded her to do.
passages.original: כְּדָת֙ מַֽה־ לַּעֲשׂ֔וֹת בַּמַּלְכָּ֖ה וַשְׁתִּ֑י עַ֣ל׀ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא־ עָשְׂתָ֗ה אֶֽת־ מַאֲמַר֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵר֔וֹשׁ בְּיַ֖ד הַסָּרִיסִֽים׃ס

passages.text: And in the presence of the king and his princes, Memucan replied, “Queen Vashti has wronged not only the king, but all the princes and the peoples in all the provinces of King Xerxes.
passages.sermon:
Memucan was one of the seven princes of Persia and Media.
He had personal access to King Xerxes.
He ranked highest in the kingdom.
Memucan spoke in front of the king and the other princes.
He said that Queen Vashti had done wrong.
He said Vashti had not only wronged the king.
He said Vashti had also wronged all the princes.
He said Vashti had also wronged all the peoples.
He said these peoples lived in all the provinces of King Xerxes.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מוּמְכָן לִפְנֵ֤י הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ וְהַשָּׂרִ֔ים לֹ֤א עַל־ הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ לְבַדּ֔וֹ עָוְתָ֖ה וַשְׁתִּ֣י הַמַּלְכָּ֑ה כִּ֤י עַל־ כָּל־ הַשָּׂרִים֙ וְעַל־ כָּל־ הָ֣עַמִּ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֕ר בְּכָל־ מְדִינ֖וֹת הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרֽוֹשׁ׃

passages.text: For the conduct of the queen will become known to all women, causing them to despise their husbands and say, ‘King Xerxes ordered Queen Vashti to be brought before him, but she did not come.’
passages.sermon:
Queen Vashti refused to obey King Xerxes.
King Xerxes commanded Queen Vashti to come before him.
Queen Vashti did not come.
All women will hear about what Queen Vashti did.
All women will know that Queen Vashti disobeyed the king.
Women will despise their husbands because of this.
Women will say, “King Xerxes ordered Queen Vashti to come, but she did not come.”
passages.original: כִּֽי־ יֵצֵ֤א דְבַר־ הַמַּלְכָּה֙ עַל־ כָּל־ הַנָּשִׁ֔ים לְהַבְז֥וֹת בַּעְלֵיהֶ֖ן בְּעֵינֵיהֶ֑ן בְּאָמְרָ֗ם הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵר֡וֹשׁ אָמַ֞ר לְהָבִ֨יא אֶת־ וַשְׁתִּ֧י הַמַּלְכָּ֛ה לְפָנָ֖יו וְלֹא־ בָֽאָה׃

passages.text: This very day the noble women of Persia and Media who have heard about the queen’s conduct will say the same thing to all the king’s officials, resulting in much contempt and wrath.
passages.sermon:
The noble women of Persia and Media have heard about Queen Vashti’s conduct.
These women will speak about it today.
They will speak to all the king’s officials.
Their words will be the same as the queen’s actions.
This will cause much contempt.
This will also cause much anger.
passages.original: וְֽהַיּ֨וֹם הַזֶּ֜ה תֹּאמַ֣רְנָה׀ שָׂר֣וֹת פָּֽרַס־ וּמָדַ֗י אֲשֶׁ֤ר שָֽׁמְעוּ֙ אֶת־ דְּבַ֣ר הַמַּלְכָּ֔ה לְכֹ֖ל שָׂרֵ֣י הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וּכְדַ֖י בִּזָּי֥וֹן וָקָֽצֶף׃

passages.text: So if it pleases the king, let him issue a royal decree, and let it be recorded in the laws of Persia and Media so that it cannot be repealed, that Vashti shall never again enter the presence of King Xerxes, and that her royal position shall be given to a woman better than she.
passages.sermon:
King Xerxes ruled over Persia and Media.
He had the power to make royal decrees.
If the king agrees, he should issue a royal command.
This command should come from the king himself.
They must write this command into the laws of Persia and Media.
No one can change these laws once they are written.
The command must say that Queen Vashti may never come before King Xerxes again.
The king must give Vashti’s royal position to another woman.
This new woman must be better than Vashti.
passages.original: אִם־ עַל־ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ ט֗וֹב יֵצֵ֤א דְבַר־ מַלְכוּת֙ מִלְּפָנָ֔יו וְיִכָּתֵ֛ב בְּדָתֵ֥י פָֽרַס־ וּמָדַ֖י וְלֹ֣א יַעֲב֑וֹר אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹֽא־ תָב֜וֹא וַשְׁתִּ֗י לִפְנֵי֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵר֔וֹשׁ וּמַלְכוּתָהּ֙ יִתֵּ֣ן הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לִרְעוּתָ֖הּ הַטּוֹבָ֥ה מִמֶּֽנָּה׃

passages.text: The edict the king issues will be heard throughout his vast kingdom—and so all women, from the least to the greatest, will honor their husbands.”
passages.sermon:
King Xerxes ruled a vast kingdom.
He planned to issue an edict.
People would hear this edict everywhere in his kingdom.
All women would hear about it.
Every woman, from the least to the greatest, would honor her husband.
passages.original: וְנִשְׁמַע֩ פִּתְגָ֨ם הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ אֲשֶֽׁר־ יַעֲשֶׂה֙ בְּכָל־ מַלְכוּת֔וֹ כִּ֥י רַבָּ֖ה הִ֑יא וְכָל־ הַנָּשִׁ֗ים יִתְּנ֤וּ יְקָר֙ לְבַעְלֵיהֶ֔ן לְמִגָּד֖וֹל וְעַד־ קָטָֽן׃

passages.text: The king and his princes were pleased with this counsel; so the king did as Memucan had advised.
passages.sermon:
King Xerxes ruled a vast kingdom.
He had many princes who advised him.
Memucan was one of these princes.
Memucan gave advice to the king.
The king listened to Memucan’s advice.
The king liked this advice.
The princes also liked this advice.
The king did what Memucan advised.
passages.original: וַיִּיטַב֙ הַדָּבָ֔ר בְּעֵינֵ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וְהַשָּׂרִ֑ים וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ כִּדְבַ֥ר מְמוּכָֽן׃

passages.text: He sent letters to all the provinces of the kingdom, to each province in its own script and to each people in their own language, proclaiming that every man should be master of his own household.
passages.sermon:
King Xerxes ruled a vast kingdom.
He sent letters to every province in his kingdom.
He sent a letter to each province in its own script.
He sent a letter to each people in their own language.
The letters said that every man should rule in his own house.
The letters said that every man should speak in the language of his own people.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח סְפָרִים֙ אֶל־ כָּל־ מְדִינ֣וֹת הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֶל־ מְדִינָ֤ה וּמְדִינָה֙ כִּכְתָבָ֔הּ וְאֶל־ עַ֥ם וָעָ֖ם כִּלְשׁוֹנ֑וֹ לִהְי֤וֹת כָּל־ אִישׁ֙ שֹׂרֵ֣ר בְּבֵית֔וֹ וּמְדַבֵּ֖ר כִּלְשׁ֥וֹן עַמּֽוֹ׃פ
